question: Which Constitutional Amendment recognised the right to form cooperative societies as a part of Fundamental Rights? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: 11th Amendment Act
99th Amendment Act
93rd Amendment Act
97th Amendment Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 97th Amendment Act

Explanation:
The 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011) granted constitutional status to cooperative societies and made the right to form them a part of Fundamental Rights. It clarified the right to form cooperative societies under Article 19(1)(c). Additionally, it added Part IX-B (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT), providing provisions for the formation, operation, and management of cooperative societies. This amendment emphasized making cooperative societies democratic, transparent, and accountable. It was a significant step towards strengthening the cooperative movement in India.

☛ Part added by 97th Amendment → Part IX-B (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT)
☛ Entry added in Concurrent List → Entry 32 (Cooperative Societies)
☛ Articles amended by 97th Amendment → Article 19(1)(c) and added Article 43-B
☛ Directive Principle for cooperative societies → Article 43-B (State shall promote voluntary formation of cooperative societies)
question_hi: किस संवैधानिक संशोधन ने सहकारी समितियों के गठन के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकारों के भाग के रूप में मान्यता दी? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)

Solution: सही उत्तर है 97वाँ संशोधन अधिनियम

Explanation:

question: Under Article 164(3) of the Constitution of India, who administers the oath of office to the State Ministers? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: President of India
Governor of the State
Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
Chief Minister of the State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor of the State

Explanation:
According to Article 164(3), the Governor of the State administers the oath of office and secrecy to State Ministers. This provision is part of the State Executive. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, appoints the Chief Minister, and on the advice of the Chief Minister, other ministers. The oath is administered in the form prescribed in the Third Schedule of the Constitution. The Governor performs this function at the state level, while the President administers oaths at the Union level.

☛ Who administers oath to the Chief Minister? → Governor (Article 164)
☛ Who administers oath to Union Ministers? → President (Article 75)
☛ Who is the head of State Council of Ministers? → Chief Minister
☛ The Third Schedule relates to? → Forms of Oaths
question_hi: भारत के संविधान के अनुच्छेद 164(3) के अंतर्गत, राज्य के मंत्रियों को पद की शपथ कौन दिलाता है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: भारत के राष्ट्रपति
राज्य के राज्यपाल
विधान सभा के अध्यक्ष
राज्य के मुख्यमंत्री
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के राज्यपाल

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 164(3) के अनुसार, राज्य के मंत्रियों को पद और गोपनीयता की शपथ राज्यपाल दिलाते हैं। यह प्रावधान राज्य कार्यपालिका का हिस्सा है। राज्यपाल संवैधानिक प्रमुख होता है और मुख्यमंत्री की नियुक्ति करता है तथा अन्य मंत्रियों की नियुक्ति मुख्यमंत्री की सलाह पर करता है। शपथ ग्रहण राज्यपाल द्वारा संविधान की तीसरी अनुसूची में निर्धारित प्रारूप में कराया जाता है। राष्ट्रपति संघ स्तर पर शपथ दिलाते हैं, जबकि राज्य स्तर पर राज्यपाल यह कार्य करते हैं।

question: Which act stated that the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay were to be subordinate to the Presidency of Bengal in all matters of war, diplomatic relations and revenue? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Charter Act of 1793
Charter Act of 1833
Pitts' lndia Act, 1784
Charter Act of 1813
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pitts' India Act, 1784

Explanation:
The Pitts' India Act of 1784 established the 'Board of Control' to oversee the affairs of the East India Company. This act made the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay subordinate to the Presidency of Bengal, especially in matters of war, diplomacy, and revenue. It was passed by the British Parliament to increase government control over the Company. The act separated the Company's political and commercial functions and gave more power to the British Crown. It was named after British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.

question: Which of the following correctly represents the three levels/tiers in the Panchayati Raj system in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Gram Sabha, Municipal Council, Cantonment Board
Gram Panchayat, Block Assemblies, State Assembly
Village Panchayat, Municipal Corporation, Zilla Parishad
Village Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zilla Parishad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Village Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zilla Parishad

Explanation:
The three levels of the Panchayati Raj system in India are: Gram Panchayat (village level), Block Samiti (intermediate level), and Zilla Parishad (district level). This system was formalized by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992), which gave constitutional status to Panchayats. Gram Panchayat is the lowest tier responsible for local development in villages. Block Samiti (Panchayat Samiti) coordinates development among multiple Gram Panchayats. Zilla Parishad is the apex body overseeing planning, finance, and development at the district level. Other options are incorrect as Gram Sabha, Municipal Council, Cantonment Board, and Municipal Corporation are not part of the Panchayati Raj structure. This system ensures decentralization and rural self-governance.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the 73rd Amendment enacted? → 1992
☛ What is the tenure of a Gram Panchayat? → 5 years
☛ Who is the head of a Block Samiti? → Pramukh or Chairperson
☛ How is Zilla Parishad constituted? → Direct elections
☛ Which is the highest tier of Panchayati Raj? → Zilla Parishad
question_hi: भारत में पंचायती राज व्यवस्था के तीन स्तरों/पर्तों को निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प सही ढंग से दर्शाता है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)

ग्राम पंचायत, नगर निगम, जिला परिषद
ग्राम पंचायत, ब्लॉक समिति, जिला परिषद
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ग्राम पंचायत, ब्लॉक समिति, जिला परिषद

Explanation:
भारत में पंचायती राज व्यवस्था के तीन स्तर हैं: ग्राम पंचायत (ग्राम स्तर), ब्लॉक समिति (मध्यवर्ती स्तर) और जिला परिषद (जिला स्तर)। यह व्यवस्था 73वें संविधान संशोधन (1992) द्वारा लागू की गई, जिसने पंचायतों को संवैधानिक दर्जा दिया। ग्राम पंचायत सबसे निचला स्तर है जो गाँवों में विकास कार्य करता है। ब्लॉक समिति (क्षेत्र समिति या पंचायत समिति) कई ग्राम पंचायतों का समूह है और विकास योजनाओं का समन्वय करती है। जिला परिषद सबसे ऊपरी स्तर है जो जिले की योजना, वित्त और विकास की देखरेख करती है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि ग्राम सभा, नगर पालिका, छावनी बोर्ड, नगर निगम पंचायती राज के अंग नहीं हैं। यह प्रणाली विकेंद्रीकरण और ग्रामीण स्वशासन को सुनिश्चित करती है।

question: Morarji Desai was commemorated on his 129th birth anniversary, 28 February 2025, for his contributions to governance reforms in India. Which of the following commissions did he chair in 1966 to restructure the country’s governance? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1st Finance Commission
1st Administrative Reforms Commission
Sarkaria Commission
Planning Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1st Administrative Reforms Commission

Explanation:
Morarji Desai chaired the 1st Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) in 1966 to restructure India's governance. The commission was established on 5 January 1966 to recommend measures for improving administrative efficiency. It submitted its report in 1970, proposing key reforms like the establishment of Lokpal, Lokayukta, and administrative tribunals. Desai was then Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. He later became Prime Minister of India in 1977. The 1st Finance Commission was formed in 1951, Sarkaria Commission in 1983, and Planning Commission in 1950.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ When was the first ARC constituted? → 5 January 1966
☛ When did the first ARC submit its report? → 1970
☛ Which commission recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta? → 1st Administrative Reforms Commission
☛ When did Morarji Desai become Prime Minister? → 1977
question_hi: 28 फ़रवरी 2025 को, भारत में शासन सुधारों में उनके योगदान के लिए मोरारजी देसाई की 129वीं जयंती मनाई गई। 1966 में देश के शासन को पुनर्गठित करने के लिए उन्होंने निम्नलिखित में से किस आयोग की अध्यक्षता की थी? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which Fundamental Right was subjected to additional restrictions by the First Amendment Act of 1951?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Right to Constitutional Remedies
Right to Freedom of Religion
Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression
Right to Equality
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression

Explanation:
The First Amendment Act of 1951 imposed additional restrictions on the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1)(a). It amended Article 19(2) to include new grounds for restriction such as public order, sovereignty and integrity of India, and friendly relations with foreign states. The amendment aimed to curb misuse of free speech and protect democracy. It also introduced the Ninth Schedule to shield land reform laws from judicial review.

question: The President's power to seek the Supreme Court's opinion on questions of law comes under ___________. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 131
Article 136
Article 226
Article 143
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 143

Explanation:
The President's power to seek the Supreme Court's opinion on questions of law comes under Article 143. This is an advisory jurisdiction, where the Court gives its opinion, which is not binding. Article 131 deals with original jurisdiction, Article 136 with special leave to appeal, and Article 226 with the power of High Courts to issue writs. The Government of India Act 1935 gave similar power to the Privy Council. The President can refer any question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its opinion.

question_hi: विधि के प्रश्नों पर सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की राय लेने की राष्ट्रपति की शक्ति ___________ के अंतर्गत आती है। (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following accurately describes the Indian President's role in foreign affairs? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: The President delegates all foreign affairs responsibilities to the Prime Minister.
The President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.
The President only receives foreign ambassadors but does not appoint them
The President is solely responsible for negotiating international treaties without any advisory input.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.

Explanation:
According to Article 53 of the Indian Constitution, the President is the Supreme Commander and head of all executive powers. In foreign affairs, the President appoints ambassadors and other diplomatic representatives in his/her name. These appointments are made on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, but formally the President performs the appointment. Additionally, the President receives foreign ambassadors, signs international treaties, and declares war and peace. However, these powers are exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Thus, option 2 is correct because the President appoints ambassadors and conducts diplomatic work in his/her name.

☛ Purpose of President's foreign visits → Strengthening bilateral relations.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन भारत के राष्ट्रपति की विदेशी मामलों में भूमिका का सही वर्णन करता है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: The Indian High Courts Act was passed in the year ______. (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1872
1909
1861
1857
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1861

Explanation:
The Indian High Courts Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1861. This act established High Courts in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, replacing the earlier Supreme Courts and Sadar Diwani/Faujdari courts. It was a significant step towards unifying the judicial system in India. Each High Court was to consist of a Chief Justice and up to 15 other judges. The act was introduced after the Government of India Act 1858, which ended the rule of the East India Company. The High Courts exercised original and appellate jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within their respective provinces.

question: Which of the following statements best describes the Indian Union Cabinet’s role in legislation? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Cabinet is the only law-making body in India.
The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.
The Cabinet enacts laws without any involvement of any house of the Indian Parliament.
The Cabinet has judicial authority over legislations surpassing the judiciary.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Cabinet gives final shape to government bills and prepares the legislative agenda.

Explanation:
The Indian Union Cabinet's legislative role involves giving final shape to government bills and preparing the legislative agenda for Parliament. The Cabinet does not enact laws itself; it discusses and approves bills before they are introduced in Parliament. It is a part of the executive branch, not the legislature. In India, legislative power rests with Parliament, which consists of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. The Cabinet guides the legislative process, but the final approval lies with Parliament. Judicial review of legislation is the domain of the judiciary, not the Cabinet. Thus, the Cabinet's role is limited to policy formulation and bill preparation.

question: How many functional items are listed in the Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution for Panchayats? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2)

question: How many times may the President of India ask the Prime Minister to have an executive recommendation reconsidered by the Cabinet? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Twice
Only once
As many times as needed
It is at the President's absolute discretion without limits.
solution:

Explanation:
According to Article 74 of the Indian Constitution, the President can ask the Cabinet to reconsider an executive recommendation only once. This constitutional provision sets a limit. If the Cabinet reaffirms the same advice after reconsideration, the President is bound to accept it. This ensures the supremacy of the executive in the parliamentary system and keeps the President as a ceremonial head. This rule was clarified by the 42nd Amendment.

question: The award (decision) made by the Lok Adalats is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and is final and binding on all parties because: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: An appeal can be filed in the Supreme Court
A review petition can be filed
An appeal can be filed in the High Court
No appeal is permissible
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is No appeal is permissible

Explanation:
Lok Adalat's award is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and is final and binding because no appeal lies against it. Lok Adalat is an alternative dispute resolution mechanism where cases are settled with mutual consent. Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, the award of a Lok Adalat has the force of a decree and is not appealable. Although in exceptional cases, a Special Leave Petition may be filed in the Supreme Court, but as a rule, no appeal is permitted. This ensures speedy and final settlement of disputes, avoiding prolonged litigation. The parties voluntarily submit to the jurisdiction of Lok Adalat, making the binding nature of the award essential.

question: Where can people of Indian origin living abroad apply for Indian citizenship under Article 8? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Indian Embassy in Delhi only
Indian Embassy at their country of living
Supreme Court
State government office
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indian Embassy at their country of living

Explanation:
Under Article 8 of the Indian Constitution, people of Indian origin living abroad who wish to obtain Indian citizenship can apply at the Indian Embassy or Consulate in the country where they reside. This provision is part of Part II of the Constitution, which deals with Citizenship. Article 8 specifically applies to persons of Indian origin who migrated from India before January 26, 1950. Therefore, they do not need to travel to Delhi or any other specific location; they can submit their application at the Indian diplomatic mission in their country of residence. This ensures ease of access for such individuals.

question: What major tax reform was introduced by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which Fundamental Right was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 specifically for children? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Right to travel abroad
Right to free electricity
Right of children to free and compulsory education
Right to vote
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Right of children to free and compulsory education

Explanation:
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 was enacted to introduce the fundamental right to education for children in India. It added Article 21A, which guarantees free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years. Additionally, it amended Article 45 and inserted Article 51A(k), making it a fundamental duty of parents to provide opportunities for education to their children. This right is part of Part III of the Constitution under Fundamental Rights. Subsequently, the Right to Education Act (RTE Act) was passed in 2009 to enforce this right. This amendment made education a fundamental right, ensuring that every child has access to schooling without any cost.

question: When appointing Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, the President of India acts on the advice of which body? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 1)

The Election Commission
The Union Council of ministers
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Union Council of ministers

Explanation:
The President of India appoints Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers. This provision is governed by Articles 155 and 156 of the Indian Constitution. The Governor acts as the representative of the President at the state level. Their appointment is made by the central government. The normal term of a Governor is five years, but they can be removed earlier by the President. The Union Council of Ministers advises the President on these appointments, and such advice is binding on the President. This ensures that the central executive has control over the appointment of constitutional heads of states.

question: Which landmark case first established the principle of judicial review in constitutional law? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Marbury v. Madison (1803)
Minerva Mills Case (1980)
Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
McCulloch v. Maryland (1819)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marbury v. Madison (1803)

Explanation:
The principle of judicial review in constitutional law was first established in the landmark U.S. Supreme Court case Marbury v. Madison (1803). In this case, Chief Justice John Marshall wrote the opinion, declaring that any law that conflicts with the Constitution is void, and it is the duty of the judiciary to invalidate such laws. William Marbury had petitioned for his judicial commission, but the Court ruled that a part of the Judiciary Act of 1789 was unconstitutional. This case laid the foundation for judicial review, empowering the judiciary to check the constitutionality of actions by the legislative and executive branches. It established the judiciary as a co-equal branch of government and solidified the system of checks and balances.

question: What is the Forty-Second Amendment of the Indian Constitution commonly known as? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Mini-Constitution
Major Bill
Mini-Parliament
Constitutional Guide
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mini-Constitution

Explanation:
The Forty-Second Amendment (1976) to the Indian Constitution is commonly known as the Mini-Constitution. Brought by the Indira Gandhi government, it was the most comprehensive amendment, introducing widespread changes. It added the words Socialist, Secular, and Integrity to the Preamble. It introduced Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) and curtailed judicial review, enhancing Parliament's supremacy. The amendment was passed during the Emergency (1975-77). Many of its provisions were later repealed by the 44th Amendment in 1978. The amendment also increased the power of the central government and made directive principles overriding fundamental rights in some cases.

question: Which of the following acts reduced the number of directors of East India Company? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (16/06/2025) Shift 2)

Charter Act of 1813

question: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers under Article 75(4) of the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister
Vice President
President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President of India

Explanation:
Under Article 75(4) of the Indian Constitution, the President of India administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Union Ministers. This oath is prescribed in the Third Schedule of the Constitution. The President is the head of the Union executive, and all ministers function in the President's name. The Council of Ministers is also appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. Only after taking the oath can a minister assume their duties. This process is a crucial step in the formation of the government, ensuring constitutional adherence and accountability.

question: Which provision was introduced in the Constitution of India through the 74th Amendment Act? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Part X
Part IX
Part IX-A
Part XI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part IX-A

Explanation:
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 introduced Part IX-A and Articles 243-P to 243-ZG in the Indian Constitution. This amendment provides constitutional status to Municipalities (urban local self-government). It provides for three types of Municipalities: Municipal Corporation (for larger urban areas), Municipal Council (for smaller urban areas), and Nagar Panchayat (for areas in transition from rural to urban). The Act also provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women. Part IX deals with Panchayats (73rd Amendment), while Part IX-A deals with Municipalities.

options_hi: भाग X
भाग IX
भाग IX-A
भाग XI
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भाग IX-A

Explanation:
74वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 द्वारा भारतीय संविधान में भाग IX-A और अनुच्छेद 243-P से 243-ZG जोड़े गए। यह संशोधन नगरपालिकाओं (शहरी स्थानीय स्वशासन) को संवैधानिक दर्जा देता है। इसके तहत तीन प्रकार की नगरपालिकाएँ प्रावधानित हैं: नगर निगम (बड़े शहरों के लिए), नगरपालिका परिषद (छोटे शहरों के लिए) और नगर पंचायत (ग्रामीण-शहरी संक्रमण क्षेत्रों के लिए)। इस अधिनियम में अनुसूचित जाति, अनुसूचित जनजाति और महिलाओं के लिए सीटों के आरक्षण का भी प्रावधान है। भाग IX ग्राम पंचायतों (73वें संशोधन) से संबंधित है, जबकि भाग IX-A नगरपालिकाओं से संबंधित है।

question: What is Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay best known for in the context of British India?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Drafting the Indian Penal Code and promoting English education
Framing the Government of India Act, 1858
Introducing the Vernacular Press Act
Leading the revolt of 1857
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Drafting the Indian Penal Code and promoting English education

Explanation:
Lord Macaulay is best known for his education policy (1835) and drafting the Indian Penal Code (IPC). He advocated for English as the medium of instruction in India, aiming to create 'a class of persons Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect.' His Minute on Education (1835) laid the foundation for Western education in India. Additionally, he is credited with drafting the Indian Penal Code, which came into effect in 1860 and remains the basis of criminal justice in India.
